discussions.title: Where do I enter my licence key? (I can't find the orange box)
discussions.body:
I bought a practice exam and got my licence key by email. The email told me to enter the key in the "orange activation box" on the practice page.

I can't find any orange box on the page. Where do I actually enter the key?
discussions.bodyHTML:
I bought a practice exam and got my licence key by email. The email told me to enter the key in the "orange activation box" on the practice page.

I can't find any orange box on the page. Where do I actually enter the key?

nodes.body:
Short version: **there is no orange box on the website.** That wording in our purchase email was our mistake. It's now fixed — sorry for the confusion.

The orange box is in the **email**, and it's simply where your key is *printed*. On the practice page, look for the **"Already purchased?"** panel with an **"Activate licence key"** button. (This used to be a small, easy-to-miss link — we replaced it on 25 August 2026.)

Here's the whole thing, start to finish.

---

### 1. Find your key

Your key arrives in **its own email — not the Stripe receipt**. The Stripe receipt is just proof of payment and never contains the key.

| | |
|---|---|
| **From** | `noreply@aguidetocloud.com` (sender name: **Guided**) |
| **Subject** | **Your licence key for …** — e.g. *"Your licence key for AI-200 Practice Exam — 1 Year Access"* |
| **Look for** | An orange panel headed **YOUR LICENCE KEY** |

The key looks like `GD-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`.

Can't find it? Search your mail for `from:aguidetocloud.com`, and check **Spam** and (in Gmail) the **Promotions** tab.

---

### 2. You may already be unlocked

If you're using **the same browser you bought it in**, you're unlocked automatically — you don't need the key at all. Look for the green **"All <N> questions unlocked"** row.

You only need to type the key in when you're on **another device or browser**, or if you cleared your browser data.

---

### 3. Open the practice page

Use the **Start Practicing →** button in that same email, or go to your exam page and open **Practice**.

---

### 4. Click the activation link

It's a small line sitting **above Quiz Options** (just under the Flashcards row, when that's shown). The coloured words are the button — click those.

---

### 5. Paste the key, click Activate

Paste it straight from the email rather than retyping. Then you'll see **✓ All <N> questions unlocked**, and the Domain dropdown jumps to the full question count.

> **The "Unlock All — $9" button stays on the page. That's normal.**
> It's part of the page header and doesn't disappear after you activate — it does **not** mean activation failed. The green row is the real confirmation.

---

### If something doesn't work

| What you see | What to do |
|---|---|
| **"I can't find the orange box"** | There isn't one on the site. The orange box is in your *email* — it's where the key is shown. On the site, look for the **"Already purchased?"** panel with the **"Activate licence key"** button, above **Quiz Options**. |
| **"Licence key not found. Please check and try again."** | Almost always a typo. Copy and paste straight from the email, and watch for a trailing space. |
| **"Invalid licence key format. Expected: GD-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX"** | Paste the whole key including the `GD-` prefix — three groups of four after it. |
| **"This key has reached its 3-device limit."** | Each key covers 3 devices. Email us and we'll reset it. |
| **"This licence key has expired."** | Access runs 12 months from purchase. Email us if that looks wrong. |
| **I don't see the activation link at all** | It's hidden when you're **already unlocked** in that browser — look for the green "All <N> questions unlocked" row instead. It's also hidden on free exams (like AZ-900), which need no key. |
| **It worked yesterday, now I'm locked again** | Access is stored in your browser, so clearing site data or using a **private/incognito** window wipes it. Just re-enter the key — usually this won't use up one of your 3, because we recognise the same device. |
| **I want it on my laptop *and* my phone** | Enter the same key on each. You get 3 devices. |
| **I paid but never got the email** | Check Spam and Gmail's Promotions tab, and search `from:aguidetocloud.com`. Still nothing — email us from the address you paid with and we'll resend it. |

---

### Good to know

- **No account, no password.** Your licence key *is* your access — keep the email and you can restore it any time.
- **3 devices**, **12 months** from purchase.
- Still stuck? Email **aguidetocloud@gmail.com** from the address you paid with.

is there any likelihood of content for the AB410 exam will be added?

From: Tamara Lewis · Related Tool: Cert Study Guides · Category: 📝 Content Idea · Reply contact provided via form

nodes.body:
Hi Tamara — thank you for this, genuinely. Short answer: **yes, and it's live now.** AB-410 has a full study guide and a 250-question practice exam as of today.

**Your nudge is the reason it exists.** I'd looked at AB-410 more than once and talked myself out of it each time, because from a distance it looked like it overlapped with PL-400, which I already cover. Your message made me actually go and check instead of assuming — and it doesn't overlap. Microsoft positions AB-410 as the replacement for **PL-200**, which is a different thing entirely. So: I was wrong, you were right to ask, and it's built.

## What's there now

- **[AB-410 cert page](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/cert-tracker/ab-410/)** — the best place to start
- **[Study guide](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/guided/ab-410/)** — 15 modules across the three official skill areas
- **[Practice exam](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/guided/ab-410/practice/)** — 250 questions
- **[First module, free, no sign-up](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/guided/ab-410/domain-1/getting-started/)** — if you just want to see whether it's any good

I've weighted the questions the way Microsoft weights the exam, rather than splitting them evenly:

| Skill area | Microsoft's weight | Questions |
|---|---|---|
| Create a foundation for intelligent applications | 25–30% | 70 |
| Create intelligent applications | 25–30% | 70 |
| Build business application logic and automation | 40–45% | 110 |

Domain 3 is nearly half the exam, so it gets nearly half the practice.

## One thing that's genuinely time-sensitive

If you're coming to AB-410 from PL-200, this matters this week. Microsoft's [Power Platform Functional Consultant Associate page](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/certifications/power-platform-functional-consultant-associate/) carries a warning that reads:

> "This certification, related exam, and renewal assessments will retire on **August 31, 2026**. You will no longer be able to earn or renew this certification after this date."

That's a week away.

Slightly annoyingly, the [PL-200 exam page](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/certifications/exams/pl-200/) still shows **"Retirement date: none"** — the two Microsoft pages disagree with each other. I'd trust the warning banner, not the blank field. Flagging it because if you'd only read the exam page you'd think you had all the time in the world.

## And the reason this one actually needed building

Microsoft's own free practice assessment for AB-410 **isn't out yet**. Their [credential page](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/certifications/intelligent-applications-builder-associate/) says one is *"usually available within 8 weeks of the exam being out of beta and generally available."* So at the moment there's no official question set to rehearse against, which is exactly the gap you pointed at.

For a proper rehearsal, use the longest run you can — the real exam gives you **120 minutes**, so a 20-question sprint won't tell you much about pacing or fatigue.

## Being straight with you on a few things

- **Cost:** the first module and 20 practice questions are free. The full 250-question bank is a **$9 one-off** — no subscription, no renewal.
- **Where it comes from:** every word is written from Microsoft's published skills outline and documentation. It doesn't reproduce real exam content, and it never will.
- **Status:** AB-410 is generally available, not beta, and has **no retirement date announced** — so it's a safe thing to invest study time in.
- **It's new.** It went live today. New material always has rough edges, and I'd rather hear about them than not.

If you work through it and something is wrong, thin, or just irritating, come back and tell me — that's exactly how this one got built in the first place.

Thanks again for the nudge.

— Sush

nodes.body:
Hi — thanks for flagging this. You found a real bug, not a missing feature, and you're the first person to spot it.

**Short answer: the counter was always there, you just couldn't see it.**

In fullscreen the quiz has a toolbar across the top showing `Q 4/50`, a progress bar, your timer, your running score and the Exit button. On desktop that whole toolbar was being drawn *underneath* the site's navigation bar, so it was completely invisible. On a phone you'd have seen your position at the bottom of the screen; on a laptop you'd have seen nothing at all. So "I don't know the stage I'm in" was exactly right — there was genuinely nothing on screen telling you.

**The cause was mine, and it was a layering mistake.** The fullscreen quiz panel sat on a lower stacking layer than the site header, so the header painted straight over the top of it. The quiz's own toolbar never stood a chance — it was trapped underneath its own container. Fixed and deployed today.

Hard-refresh the practice page (**Ctrl+Shift+R**, or **Cmd+Shift+R** on a Mac) and you should now see, across the top:

- `Q 4/50` — where you are in the run
- a progress bar
- your timer
- your running score
- the Exit button

Two things came out of it that I'd rather tell you than quietly fix. The **five-minute warning** was being hidden by exactly the same bug, so that's back as well. And I've added an automated check that now runs before every release — if that toolbar is ever covered again, the build fails instead of shipping. This one survived as long as it did precisely because nothing was watching for it.

**One question back to you**, because your wording could mean two different things:

1. **The position indicator at the top** — that's what's now fixed, or
2. **A number on the question card itself** — e.g. "Question 4 of 50" sitting just above the question text.

If you meant 2, or you'd like both, say so and I'll add it. It's a small change and it's a fair ask.

One last thing, in case it looks like a second bug: **Question Map · 3/50 answered** counts the questions you've *answered*, not where you are. If you skip ahead with Next it deliberately won't move. The `Q 4/50` counter is the one that tracks your position.

Thanks again for taking the time to write it up.

— Sush

nodes.body:
Hi Jens — congratulations, and thank you. Passing your first ever IT exam while changing careers is a big thing. Coming back afterwards to tell me where my guide fell short is the most useful thing anyone has done for this site all month.

Four things in your message, in order.

## 1. The automation questions — you didn't miss anything. That one was on me.

You were right, and I checked. Microsoft updated the MD-102 blueprint on **24 July 2026** and added a fifth skill area: *"Optimize endpoint operations by using automation, monitoring, and reporting"* — 10–15% of the exam. My study guide was still built around the old four areas, so a tenth to a sixth of the published blueprint simply wasn't in it.

It's now built. Five new modules, plus 30 new practice questions on exactly that material (the bank is now 280 rather than 250), and I corrected the domain weightings across the course — they were still showing the old split, which would have had you studying to the wrong proportions.

- [Graph & PowerShell automation](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/guided/md-102/domain-5/graph-powershell-automation/)
- [Security Copilot agents in Intune](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/guided/md-102/domain-5/security-copilot-agents/)
- [Intune reporting & workbooks](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/guided/md-102/domain-5/intune-reporting-workbooks/)
- [Endpoint analytics & remediations](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/guided/md-102/domain-5/endpoint-analytics-remediations/)
- [Tenant health & alerting](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/guided/md-102/domain-5/tenant-health-alerts/)

Two honest caveats. Microsoft also changed things *inside* the four existing areas in that same update, and I haven't finished working through those yet — Domain 5 was the big hole and it's closed, the rest is next. And all of it is written from Microsoft's published skills outline and documentation; it doesn't reproduce recalled or disclosed exam content, and it never will.

One thing that moves fast here: some Security Copilot agents are still in preview, and the [Device Offboarding Agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/copilot/agents/device-offboarding-agent) stopped being available on **1 June 2026**. I wrote that into the module rather than quietly dropping it, because Microsoft's general agents overview still lists it while the agent's own page carries the retirement notice — so you'll meet the stale answer elsewhere.

## 2. Practice length — yes, go longer.

Microsoft's [exam duration page](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/support/exam-duration-exam-experience) puts Associate exams without labs at **100 minutes**, and says most exams *"typically contain between 40-60 questions."* So a 20-question run is a third to a half of the real thing, with none of the fatigue.

For a proper rehearsal, use **50 questions + 90 minutes** — 90 is the longest timer available, and that lands you near real pacing. There's also an **All** option in the question-count buttons if you ever want the entire bank. One thing I'd rather say plainly than have it read as a sales pitch: the free practice is capped at 20 questions, so those longer runs need the $9 unlock.

Ignore one thing while you do it: my 80% pass bar is not Microsoft's 700. Microsoft's 700 is a *scaled* score, not a percentage, so it doesn't convert. Treat 80% as a safety margin.

**But length isn't really what you're getting at.** The harder part is reasoning about how things interact — which assignment wins, what a conflict does, what a grace period changes. And that's a fair hit on my question bank: too many of my questions ask what a feature *is*, and not enough set up a small environment and ask what *happens*. That's on me, and it's going on the list.

Two things that help more than a longer timer:

- When you get a question right, make yourself say *why the other options are wrong* before moving on. Every multiple-choice, true/false and multi-select question has a "why wrong" note for exactly that.
- Build the scenario for real in a trial tenant. Two groups, two conflicting profiles, one device. Watching a conflict actually happen teaches it in a way no question can.

## 3. MS-102 — the date matters, and it isn't October.

It's **30 November 2026**, and it applies to both the **MS-102 exam** and the **Microsoft 365 Certified: Administrator Expert** certification it leads to. MS-102 is on [Microsoft's exam retirement list](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/support/retired-certification-exams), and the Expert certification is on the [credential retirement page](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/support/credential-retirement). So you have more runway than you thought — but it's a real deadline.

Two things worth knowing before you decide:

- **You already hold the prerequisite.** Earning the Expert certification takes two things: passing MS-102, and holding at least one of four Associate certifications. [Endpoint Administrator Associate](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/certifications/modern-desktop/) — the one you just earned — is one of the four. That prerequisite gates *earning the Expert credential*, not *sitting the exam*; you don't need a prerequisite certification to book MS-102.
- **MS-102 is not a top-up on MD-102.** Its four areas are Microsoft 365 tenant administration, Microsoft Entra identity and access, threat protection with Microsoft Defender XDR, and compliance with Microsoft Purview. Exchange, Teams and SharePoint aren't standalone areas — their tasks are spread across those four. It's a genuinely different study effort, not a victory lap.

And if you do earn it before the deadline, it stays on your transcript under **Active Certifications** until it expires, then moves to **Historical Certifications**. It doesn't vanish.

## 4. On "no path to professional" — you've spotted something real.

You're right that AB-650 is Associate level. But the published pathway is changing, and that's worth understanding before you pick a direction. The Expert rung above MS-102 retires on 30 November 2026 and the MS-102 exam retires with it. Meanwhile [AB-650](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/certifications/exams/ab-650/) is in **beta** and leads to a new certification, **Microsoft 365 Certified: AI Services Administrator Associate (beta)** — roughly a quarter tenant and workload administration, a little under half governance and security, and **35–40% managing and securing AI services**. That new line has no retirement date listed.

So the observable position: after 30 November the Expert rung on the Microsoft 365 administration line is gone, and the newer option Microsoft points to is Associate-level. Microsoft hasn't announced an Expert-level successor. My read is that this is a timing problem rather than a dead end — but that's my read, not something Microsoft has said.

That gives you three genuinely different options rather than one blocked path:

| Option | What it gets you | The catch |
|---|---|---|
| **MS-102 before 30 Nov** | The Expert badge, the last chance to earn it | Retiring credential, hard deadline |
| **AB-650** | The newer line, heavy on Copilot and AI services | Beta, Associate-level for now |
| **SC-300 → SC-100** | A live Associate → Expert path, nothing scheduled to retire | Different role family: identity and security |

On that third one — if identity and security interests you, [SC-300](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/cert-tracker/sc-300/) is a sensible next step from where you are: Entra ID, conditional access, device identity, all things you've just been living in. It earns Identity and Access Administrator Associate, one of three certifications that can qualify you for Cybersecurity Architect Expert — you need one of the three, plus [SC-100](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/cert-tracker/sc-100/) itself. Worth knowing: one of the other two, Azure Security Engineer Associate, is itself retiring on 31 August 2026.

Honestly though, at this stage the thing that will move you furthest isn't the next badge — it's hands-on. That new automation domain is a great place to start: wire up a remediation script, poke at Intune through Graph, break something in a lab tenant. That's the stuff that strengthens your case in interviews and makes the next exam easier, and it's exactly what the new Domain 5 modules walk through.

Hi Jens — congratulations, and thank you. Passing your first ever IT exam while changing careers is a big thing. Coming back afterwards to tell me where my guide fell short is the most useful thing anyone has done for this site all month.

Four things in your message, in order.

1. The automation questions — you didn't miss anything. That one was on me.

You were right, and I checked. Microsoft updated the MD-102 blueprint on 24 July 2026 and added a fifth skill area: "Optimize endpoint operations by using automation, monitoring, and reporting" — 10–15% of the exam. My study guide was still built around the old four areas, so a tenth to a sixth of the published blueprint simply wasn't in it.

It's now built. Five new modules, plus 30 new practice questions on exactly that material (the bank is now 280 rather than 250), and I corrected the domain weightings across the course — they were still showing the old split, which would have had you studying to the wrong proportions.

  • Graph & PowerShell automation
  • Security Copilot agents in Intune
  • Intune reporting & workbooks
  • Endpoint analytics & remediations
  • Tenant health & alerting

Two honest caveats. Microsoft also changed things inside the four existing areas in that same update, and I haven't finished working through those yet — Domain 5 was the big hole and it's closed, the rest is next. And all of it is written from Microsoft's published skills outline and documentation; it doesn't reproduce recalled or disclosed exam content, and it never will.

One thing that moves fast here: some Security Copilot agents are still in preview, and the Device Offboarding Agent stopped being available on 1 June 2026. I wrote that into the module rather than quietly dropping it, because Microsoft's general agents overview still lists it while the agent's own page carries the retirement notice — so you'll meet the stale answer elsewhere.

2. Practice length — yes, go longer.

Microsoft's exam duration page puts Associate exams without labs at 100 minutes, and says most exams "typically contain between 40-60 questions." So a 20-question run is a third to a half of the real thing, with none of the fatigue.

For a proper rehearsal, use 50 questions + 90 minutes — 90 is the longest timer available, and that lands you near real pacing. There's also an All option in the question-count buttons if you ever want the entire bank. One thing I'd rather say plainly than have it read as a sales pitch: the free practice is capped at 20 questions, so those longer runs need the $9 unlock.

Ignore one thing while you do it: my 80% pass bar is not Microsoft's 700. Microsoft's 700 is a scaled score, not a percentage, so it doesn't convert. Treat 80% as a safety margin.

But length isn't really what you're getting at. The harder part is reasoning about how things interact — which assignment wins, what a conflict does, what a grace period changes. And that's a fair hit on my question bank: too many of my questions ask what a feature is, and not enough set up a small environment and ask what happens. That's on me, and it's going on the list.

  • When you get a question right, make yourself say why the other options are wrong before moving on. Every multiple-choice, true/false and multi-select question has a "why wrong" note for exactly that.
  • Build the scenario for real in a trial tenant. Two groups, two conflicting profiles, one device. Watching a conflict actually happen teaches it in a way no question can.

discussions.body:
Can MS Teams as part of Microsoft Business Basic enable chatting with external users?

---
**Category:** 💡 Feature Request
discussions.bodyHTML:
Can MS Teams as part of Microsoft Business Basic enable chatting with external users?

Category: 💡 Feature Request

nodes.body:
Hi — thanks for asking. Good news: this one already exists, so there's nothing to build. 🙂

**Short answer: yes** — as long as your Business Basic plan is one of the versions that includes Teams (more on that in a second). Chatting with people outside your organisation is a standard part of Teams, not an enterprise-only extra, and it's **on by default**.

**In most cases you don't need to change a single setting.** Open Teams, start a new chat, and type the person's **full email address** — if they're in another Microsoft 365 organisation, it usually just connects. The feature is called **external access** (or federation), and the default setting is **Allow all external domains**.

**The one thing to confirm first:** Business Basic is now sold in a **"with Teams"** and a **"without Teams"** version. If you're on the without-Teams one, you'd need Teams alongside it — **Teams Essentials** is about $4/user/month (USD, annual). Worth checking in the Microsoft 365 admin centre before anything else, because that's the only situation where the answer is "no". ([Compare Teams plans](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-teams/compare-microsoft-teams-options) · [my Business Basic notes](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/licensing/microsoft-365-business-basic/))

---

**What external chat can and can't do**

You get 1:1 and group chat, calls, meetings, video and presence with people in other organisations. Screen sharing works too, though it's most reliable in a 1:1 chat between two Teams work accounts.

⚠️ What it **can't** do: **share files**, or give the other person access to your teams, channels or SharePoint sites. It's conversation only — that catches people out, so it's worth knowing up front.

Admin controls live at **Teams admin center → Users → External access**.
📄 [Manage external meetings and chat](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/trusted-organizations-external-meetings-chat)

**If you do need to swap files**, there are two other routes — both included with Business Basic's Teams:

- **Guest access** — invite someone *into* a team so they can see files and channel conversations. Guests don't use one of your Microsoft 365 licences, though heavy guest usage can attract a small Microsoft Entra External ID charge above the free tier. Set up in **Users → Guest access**, plus matching sharing settings in Entra ID, Microsoft 365 Groups and SharePoint — it's the fiddliest of the three, because the switches live in several places. 📄 [Guest access in Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/guest-access)
- **Shared channels (Teams Connect)** — one channel both organisations work in, using their own accounts, with no guest account created. Needs an Entra admin in *both* organisations to set up cross-tenant trust, so it depends on the other side's cooperation.

---

**If chat isn't working, the order I'd check:**

1. **Both sides have to say yes.** Federation is two-way. If the other organisation blocks yours, or hasn't enabled external access for that person, chat quietly fails no matter what you set on your end.
2. **Careful with the allow list.** If you add even one domain to the **allowed** list, **every other domain is blocked** — people add a partner's domain and accidentally cut off everyone else. To block just a few, use the **blocked** list instead.
3. **Personal Microsoft accounts are a separate toggle** on the same page (on by default in commercial tenants, but not available in GCC, GCC High or DoD).
4. **Trial-only tenants are blocked by default** — if either side is on a trial, someone has to change it.

📄 The comparison table I'd bookmark: [External access vs guest access, side by side](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/communicate-with-users-from-other-organizations)

If you tell me what you're actually trying to do — just chat with a client, or properly collaborate on files with them — I'll point you at the right one. 🙂

— Sush

discussions.title: [💬 General] Negative prompting should not have to be a thing
discussions.body:
One of my biggest bug bears with Copilot is the need to use "negative prompting" to get accurate responses and stop it assuming or editorialising when it is not asked to. It even admits this and when using advanced prompts to get it to critique its own answers it seems to come up with a multitude of examples of this and advise that: "I understand the frustration. From a user perspective, "reformat this document" should not require you to also say:
•	don't add content
•	don't summarise
•	don't invent email addresses
•	don't change meaning
•	don't rewrite policy
•	don't claim validation you didn't do
Those should be the default assumptions. What you're describing is a known usability problem in AI systems generally: users end up learning to write defensive prompts because the model is optimising for being helpful, comprehensive, and proactive. Unfortunately, in document work, "proactive" can easily become "made changes I never asked for. In other words, the burden should be on the system to understand the risk profile of the task, not on the user to write increasingly restrictive instructions.
The specific business risk I think you're identifying is:
The system can cross the boundary between presentation changes and content changes without making that boundary sufficiently obvious to the user. That's particularly important in environments like Oranga Tamariki, where documents can contain operational guidance, legal references, care decisions, privacy-sensitive information, and instructions that staff may rely on.  If the system changes content while improving appearance, the visual quality can mask the fact that substantive changes have occurred. That's a governance risk, not just a quality issue. So, I don't think the lesson is "users need better prompts." That's particularly important in environments like Oranga Tamariki, where documents can contain operational guidance, legal references, care decisions, that staff may rely on."   Isn't this supposed to save time?

nodes.body:
Hi Julio — thanks for the detail and the linked issue, that really helps pin it down.

The key clue is in your own note: `gh auth login` works fine in PowerShell, but Scout still says it "could not verify your GitHub sign-in state." That's a different failure from the usual "ask your admin to enable Scout" gate — your org side is fine; the block is on the **GitHub-verify** step, which runs *after* your Microsoft 365 sign-in succeeds. It almost always means Scout is reading a **different GitHub identity — or an un-authorised token — than the seat you expect.**

I've just added a dedicated section to the setup guide walking through it end to end:
👉 **[GitHub sign-in could not be completed — troubleshooting](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/blog/microsoft-scout-admin-install-frontier-enrollment/#github-sign-in-could-not-be-completed)**

The short version, in the order I'd check:
1. **Same account everywhere** — the GitHub login Scout uses must be the exact one holding your Copilot seat *and* the one `gh` uses (personal-vs-work mismatch is the #1 cause).
2. **Authorise the token for SSO** — if your org enforces SAML SSO, a login can succeed while the token stays un-authorised: `gh auth login`, then `gh auth refresh -h github.com`, and **authorise your org** when prompted.
3. **Reset gh** — `gh auth logout` → `gh auth login` (GitHub.com → HTTPS → browser) → retry in Scout.
4. **Clear stale Windows credentials** — Credential Manager → Windows Credentials → remove old `github.com` entries → retry.
5. **Confirm the Copilot Business seat is actually *assigned* to your GitHub login** (not just available in the org).

If all five are clean and it still fails, it's server-side — keep [scout-resources#17](https://github.com/microsoft/scout-resources/issues/17) open, since that's the official channel to the Scout team (my site is an independent guide, so I can't push a product fix). Let me know which step it dies on and I'll dig in further. 🙏

Hope that unblocks them!

nodes.body:
Hi Billy,

Thanks for the detail — you've done the hard parts already, and you're closer than it feels. One reframe first (it catches a lot of people, and your message exposed a gap in my own guide that I've just fixed — so thank you):

**The error is the "organisation enabled" gate, and Scout signs in to Microsoft 365 *before* the GitHub step.** So it most likely points to the Microsoft 365 / Frontier / Intune admin setup — **not** your GitHub license. To your direct question: **no, you don't need to rush to a paid GitHub Enterprise plan.** Scout needs GitHub Copilot **Business or Enterprise** — Business is enough; the individual Free/Pro/Pro+ plans aren't listed as qualifying. If your Enterprise *trial* has assigned that seat to the GitHub account you sign in with, it should work while the trial's active (worth verifying the seat in your GitHub org's Copilot settings). But that's only checked later, at the separate "Sign in to GitHub" step — not where you're stuck.

**On the attestation — "no response yet" is expected.** Microsoft's docs describe that step as completing the form to *record* your opt-in; they don't mention an approval reply coming back. So don't treat "no response" as your blocker.

**So where's the real blocker?** In order:

1. **Wait it out** — the *Copilot Frontier* save takes **up to ~3 hours** to apply. Fully quit Scout and relaunch.
2. **Is *your own* account in scope?** If you set Frontier to *Specific users*, your sign-in account must be in that list. Easiest while testing: switch to *All users*.
3. **M365 Copilot license** on the exact account you sign in with.
4. **Did the Intune policy reach your PC?** "Set in Intune" ≠ "applied on the device." On the PC: *Settings → Accounts → Access work or school → your account → Info → Sync*, then relaunch Scout.

Hey Dean — thanks for flagging this, great spot.

I've just updated the page with a [proper M365 E5 section](https://www.aguidetocloud.com/licensing/security-copilot/) (give Cloudflare ~2 min to deploy).

**Quick answer for the page-update record:**

Security Copilot is **NOT bundled with M365 E5** — it's a standalone pay-per-use product at $4 per Security Compute Unit (SCU) per hour.

That said, E5 customers are the natural buyer. Security Copilot's superpower is reasoning across signals it doesn't generate itself — and E5 is what provides those signals:

| E5 component | What Security Copilot uses it for |
|---|---|
| Defender XDR (endpoint, email, identity, cloud apps) | Cross-workload incident investigation |
| Entra ID P2 | User risk + conditional access context |
| Purview | Insider risk + DLP correlation |
| Intune | Device compliance signals |

Microsoft Sentinel is the one most people get caught by — Sentinel is **NOT in E5**, it's billed separately by GB ingested. You can still use Security Copilot without Sentinel, but cross-source threat hunting gets much weaker.

**Microsoft Learn references (added to the page):**
- [Security Copilot overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/security/microsoft-security-copilot)
- [Getting started](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/security/get-started-security-copilot)
- [Manage SCU usage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/security/manage-usage)
